prompt.brief: Design a multi-tenant IoT platform that securely onboards millions of devices, ingests telemetry, supports commands, processes streams, and exposes anomaly-aware device operations.
successSignals: Define device identity, provisioning, heartbeat, telemetry envelope, ordering, QoS, command acknowledgment, tenant isolation, and retention.
Partition ingestion by tenant/device and time, handle reconnect storms, duplicates, offline buffering, backpressure, and out-of-order events.
Separate the device gateway from durable telemetry, stream processing, time-series queries, digital-twin state, and command delivery.
Explain certificate rotation, fleet rollouts, anomaly detection, regional failure, cost controls, observability, and degraded operation.

functional: Provision devices and credentials, accept telemetry, expose current and historical readings, and maintain device/twin status.
Process windows for alerts and anomalies, provide tenant dashboards, and send authenticated commands with delivery status.
Support firmware rollout rings, revocation, device deletion, replay, offline reconnect, and recovery from partial regional outages.
nonFunctional: Accept telemetry with p95 gateway acknowledgment under 200ms and surface stream alerts within 10 seconds.
Scale to 10M connected devices and reconnect storms without a single hot key or unbounded synchronous work.
Do not lose committed state; make retries and duplicate events safe.
Degrade safely when downstream workers, caches, or external dependencies fail.
scaleAssumptions: 10M devices sending an average of one message per minute, with 10x reconnect bursts
Partition by the primary tenant, user, item, or geographic key and isolate hot partitions.
Keep serving state bounded; retain raw events or durable records for replay and auditing.

dataFlow.title: Accept Connect millions of IoT devices
dataFlow.description: The Multi-tenant IoT platform gateway authenticates the caller, validates the request, applies tenant policy and idempotency, then routes it to the owning service.

dataFlow.title: Commit the durable state
dataFlow.description: The Multi-tenant IoT platform service records the accepted state and version before acknowledging the client.

dataFlow.title: Publish the domain event
dataFlow.description: A durable outbox publishes committed Multi-tenant IoT platform events; consumers deduplicate by event ID and track offsets.

dataFlow.description: Partitioned workers consume Multi-tenant IoT platform events, update the serving projection, and expose lag or watermark metadata.

dataFlow.description: Serving reads use the Multi-tenant IoT platform projection; replay, repair, export, and slow work remain off the request path.

deepDives.title: Consistency and idempotency
points: Keep the Multi-tenant IoT platform commit authoritative; let derived projections converge with visible version and freshness.
Use idempotency keys, conditional Multi-tenant IoT platform writes, event IDs, and versions so retries and replay are safe.
Return Multi-tenant IoT platform version and observedAt so clients can reason about freshness.

deepDives.title: Partitioning and hot keys
points: Partition Multi-tenant IoT platform by its primary read and write keys, then isolate hot tenants, users, items, or regions.
Bound Multi-tenant IoT platform work with backpressure and queue isolation so one hot key cannot dominate the cluster.
Keep a replay or reconciliation path for Multi-tenant IoT platform projection drift and partial failures.

deepDives.title: Failure and recovery
points: Serve the last acceptable Multi-tenant IoT platform projection or an explicit degraded response when workers fail.
Retain durable Multi-tenant IoT platform records for replay and make each downstream effect independently retryable.
Measure Multi-tenant IoT platform latency, backlog, freshness, error rate, and correctness drift.

tradeoffs.title: Strong consistency versus throughput
tradeoffs.recommendation: Strongly protect the business commit and use versioned eventual projections for high-volume reads.
tradeoffs.caution: Making every derived read synchronous increases coordination and tail latency.

tradeoffs.title: Push versus pull processing
tradeoffs.recommendation: Push bounded events to workers and pull durable snapshots on reads or recovery.
tradeoffs.caution: Unbounded fanout or full scans make bursts and hot keys expensive.

tradeoffs.title: Managed service versus custom control
tradeoffs.recommendation: Start with managed primitives where their limits match the access pattern, then isolate replaceable interfaces.
tradeoffs.caution: Provider defaults do not remove the need for quotas, replay, observability, and data lifecycle design.

commonMistakes: Putting all work on the synchronous request path.
Choosing a data store before writing the access patterns and consistency contract.
Ignoring retries, duplicate events, late data, deletion, privacy, or authorization.
Leaving hot partitions, backpressure, stale reads, and recovery unspecified.
Allowing unbounded requests or exports to compete with normal traffic.

followUps.question: What happens when the primary worker is unavailable?
followUps.answer: Acknowledge only after the durable boundary, serve the last acceptable projection, queue retryable work, and replay or reconcile after recovery.

followUps.question: How would you support a tenfold traffic spike?
followUps.answer: Pre-scale partitions, apply admission control and backpressure, isolate hot keys, cache immutable snapshots, and make freshness degradation visible.

followUps.question: How do you verify correctness?
followUps.answer: Use idempotency metrics, version gaps, sampled source-to-projection comparisons, replay tests, and a shadow rebuild before repair.

rubric.description: The answer defines the Connect millions of IoT devices workflow, scale, latency, durability, and failure contract.

Entities and keys support Design an IoT platform that connects millions of devices, ingests sensor data at scale, processes streams in real-time, and detects anomalies., authorization, privacy, and lifecycle changes.
Partitioning, cache behavior, queues, backpressure, and hot-key handling are explicit.
Idempotency, replay, recovery, degraded reads, and observability protect committed state.
The candidate can explain Multi-tenant IoT platform consistency, push/pull, managed services, and the scale boundary.
